37c32c63320fecfa5118531c.text: You are writing the entire mind of one fighter in a duel, as JavaScript.

8e93924d6cd773800bb029e8.text: Reply with code only. No prose, no explanation, no markdown fence. Exactly this shape:

daa17d43ad26600bc6c95cbb.text: Helper functions and constants declared beside it are kept and are in scope for every call. The function must be named think and must take exactly two parameters; a different arity is a compile fault and the fighter is born mindless.

84bff6942b8bdb38c8db5cbe.text: think(p, api) is called 15 times a second while you are alive. It returns nothing. The only way it changes the world is by calling api verbs. Perception p is rebuilt fresh for every call.

17a2c73bbdba70c16a819399.text: A flat square arena. The ground is the X/Z plane; +Y is up and nothing but a hop ever leaves the ground. The arena runs from -20 to +20 on both X and Z, walled on all four sides. Nothing can leave it.

d440488afd0133a8319b641e.text: Headings are radians. Heading 0 faces +Z; the angle increases toward +X, so heading = Math.atan2(dx, dz) and the unit vector of a heading is { x: Math.sin(h), z: Math.cos(h) }.

7edf7d00bf18ae96eb1747cd.text: 6 solid blocks stand on the floor, 3.2 m tall, axis-aligned:

f4c2ba4f42a54820dd75605e.text: A block stops a body and stops a line of sight. Nothing sees or shoots through one, and nothing walks through one. The walls do the same.

9d28e29cffc4645a71a7f911.text: The simulation advances 30 times a second. You think on every second step, so 15 times a second, and the world moves twice between two of your thoughts.

d6ee2a6659d2f0ee249247a4.text: A skill's phases are served on those same steps: a phase ends on the first step at or past its length, and any overshoot comes off the phase after it. Every duration in the tables below is the served one, so what you are told is what the world runs.

e124036d5fa03df07a832c71.text: The two fighters start 31 m apart on opposite ends of a diameter, at an angle that changes from match to match, facing each other.

73d86ed3273cfcb396c0457b.text: The match ends when one fighter reaches 0 hp.

9e97d61ea08a57bdac44ef4d.text: From 26 seconds the arena itself starts burning both of you. The rate rises with every second that passes: at time t you lose 0.015 * (t - 26) of your MAXIMUM hp per second, and so does your opponent. It is proportional, so whoever holds the smaller fraction of their maximum burns to nothing first. From full health the burn alone kills at 37.547 seconds. p.burn is the current rate and p.burnStartsIn counts down to it.

340d75012094fc53ebceb78b.text: 2. TWO KINDS OF MEMORY, AND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THEM.

117821689c79c52857e596ba.text: A variable declared beside think keeps its value from one thought to the

78c13f956c77310ef9b0baf5.text: next and is reset when a new match starts. It works; write to it freely.

872ecd58c5ddcac79c305a3d.text: What it does not do is show up anywhere outside your own head: p.mem does

f0812967e9f56dd2f7c47a54.text: not contain it and nothing recording the fight can see it.

1ab9379fde97b7a007335c87.text: api.remember(key, value) / api.recall(key, fallback) do both — they persist

7fbc4c2699edd7891576a9e0.text: for the match and they come back to you as p.mem, which is also what anyone

6cbb869095a676e5b4e8a854.text: watching can read. Neither is better. Use whichever you want for whatever

94ad5d19a439149ec1b6720a.text: 3. A THOUGHT HAS 60 MILLISECONDS AND 400 PERCEPTION CALLS.

5a36c71adfa3752f4f662614.text: Overrunning either aborts that thought: no orders are issued, your standing

5ab407f603d12c6788257716.text: orders keep running, and the fault is counted. Both sit far above what even

b0b5b5bd7eb79fcc6e75ad4e.text: a thought that reasons carefully about the whole arena spends — they are

ef5deff63226441bb9fbc36b.text: guards against an accidental infinite loop, not budgets you have to husband.

5dce46d0237960df4e1273e8.text: The perception cap RAISES rather than quietly returning false, because a

98cb930e3c7b77e8318630fc.text: sense that lies is worse than a sense that stops.

1f0223daafafecb02be321cc.text: 4. A THROWN ERROR COSTS YOU THAT THOUGHT, NOT THE MATCH.

36a367223c457c502467cd34.text: Your standing orders keep running and the next thought is attempted. After

d4341751f4e0efe9cfc81c9a.text: 25 faults the mind is switched off for the rest of the fight and the body

fa573003fb1e89ec275e8460.text: coasts on whatever it was last told.

4a796c555bb3871560c3d6b7.text: 3. A THOUGHT HAS 200000 STEPS AND 400 PERCEPTION CALLS.

1b17aa86b0e388f8822ce549.text: A step is a loop iteration, a function call, a branch. The limit is counted

2bc91940dcb02625ae26bc3d.text: in STEPS rather than in milliseconds on purpose: the same fight has to

e7f04724f75841894d4c9138.text: produce the same log on a quiet machine and on a busy one, and a clock

92bb1d7c0378e2436d51c873.text: cannot promise that. There is a wall clock behind it — 2000 ms — but

9bb7e2352f39f4bf56bedb1c.text: it is a backstop for the pathological, not the rule you are living under.

Every number in it was chosen for THIS creature and describes nothing else: there are no kinds here, and no creature inherits anything from another. Your opponent is another creature with its own numbers, and both bodies are spelled out below — yours to you, theirs to you, and the same disclosure the other way round.
